Every D_PDU, whatever its type, starts with the same 16-bit sync sequence.

requirement: The first 4 header bytes of every D_PDU hold the same fields.
A 4-bit D_PDU Type field identifies the D_PDU type.
A 12-bit field carries an engineering orderwire (EOW) message.
An 8-bit field carries the end of transmission (EOT) information.
One byte carries the 3-bit Size of Address Field and the 5-bit Size of Header field.
The 1 to 7 bytes after byte 3, as given by Size of Address Field, carry the source and destination addresses.
The D_PDU type-specific header part is as specified for each type in this annex.
The last two bytes of every header hold the CRC computed per C.4.2.8.
Every bit in a field specified as NOT USED is sent as zero.

requirement: D_PDU types are as defined in Table C-2 and the per-type figures.
The D_PDU type number value indicates the D_PDU type.

The 12-bit EOW field carries engineering orderwire management messages.

The first 4 bits of the EOW (bits 11-8) hold the EOW type.
The remaining 8 bits of the EOW (bits 7-0) hold the type-specific EOW data.
EOW mapping: EOW bits 11-8 go in header byte 0 bits 3-0 (EOW MSB at byte 0 bit 3); EOW bits 7-0 go in header byte 1 bits 7-0 (EOW LSB at byte 1 bit 0).
The 8-bit EOT field approximates the time remaining in the current transmission of the sending node.
notes: Used to time exchanges and cut turnaround and collisions.

requirement: EOT is an unsigned binary count of half-second intervals remaining in the current transmission, measured from the start of this D_PDU including its sync bytes.

requirement: Size of Address Field gives m, the number of bytes holding the source and destination addresses.
The address field is 1 to 7 bytes long; source and destination addresses have equal length.
Address lengths come in 4-bit steps: 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3 or 3.5 bytes.
GAP: a received header with Size of Address Field 0 is NOT STATED. Reading: treat the D_PDU as invalid and discard it silently; with no source address there is nobody to warn.
Size of Header gives h, the header length in bytes, counting the type, EOW, EOT, size byte, type-specific header and header CRC.
Size of Header excludes the address field.
Worked example: a WARNING D_PDU has h = 7 (4 fixed bytes, 1 type-specific byte, 2 CRC bytes).
notes: Header byte 3 = 0x47: m = 2, h = 7.

requirement: Every D_PDU sent carries both source and destination address, each taking half the address field bits.
The first half of the address field is the destination address.
The second half of the address field is the source address.
For odd m the middle address byte is shared: destination in its high nibble, source in its low nibble (Figure C-4(a)); for even m each address takes m/2 whole bytes (Figure C-4(b), p.C-15).
notes: Figure C-4 labels the last address row 4+m; the address ends at byte 3+m (Figure C-2, worked example p.C-19).

requirement: Addresses are binary numbers, from 4 bits up to 28 bits (3.5 bytes) each.
Each byte or fractional byte of an address is represented by a decimal number (dotted decimal).
The binary value of each dotted-decimal number is mapped into the corresponding byte.
Unicast (node) addresses run from 0.0.0.0 to 15.255.255.255.
For D_PDUs supporting group addressing (types 7 and 8), the group flag is treated as a 29th address bit, giving group addresses 16.0.0.0 to 31.255.255.255.
The broadcast (all stations) address is group address 31.255.255.255.
A fractional-byte part of an address maps to the leftmost non-zero number of the dotted-decimal form.
The other dotted-decimal numbers refer to whole-byte parts of the address.
Example: with 3.5-byte addresses written w.x.y.z, w ranges 0 to 15 and carries the top bits; z carries the bottom 8 bits.

Address bits are placed with the address MSB in the MSB of the first byte of its field and the LSB in the LSB of the last byte, per Figure C-4(a) for 0.5, 1.5, 2.5, 3.5 bytes and Figure C-4(b) for 1, 2, 3 bytes.
When any field spans several octets, bit significance decreases as octet number increases (most significant part in the first octet).
notes: General rule; see interp C-0134.

requirement: The lowest numbered bit of a field holds its lowest order value.
Leading zero address bytes may be omitted, keeping source and destination the same length.
Trailing zero address bytes are always sent.
Worked example: m = 2 with destination 0.0.0.5 and source 0.0.0.100 gives address bytes 0x05 0x64.

GAP: how a sender picks m is NOT STATED beyond dropping leading zero bytes, though lengths come in half-byte steps. Reading: send the smallest whole number of nibbles that holds both addresses (giving m = that nibble count, 1 to 7); on receipt accept any m from 1 to 7 and zero-extend.

requirement: The bytes after the address field encode the type-specific header defined in C.4.4 to C.4.15.
The header has its own 2-byte CRC so that a valid header can be used even when the data part is corrupt.
The two bytes after the type-specific header hold a 16-bit CRC.
The header CRC polynomial is x^16+x^15+x^12+x^11+x^8+x^6+x^3+1 (0x19949), computed by the V.41 Appendix I shift-register method or an equivalent software method.
notes: Not the V.41 polynomial.

requirement: The header CRC shift register starts at all zeros.
The header CRC covers every header bit except the sync: type, EOW, EOT, both size fields, addresses and the type-specific header.
A header with a valid CRC is processed whatever the result of the CRC on any segmented C_PDU in the same D_PDU.
CRC bits map into the CRC bytes with the CRC MSB in the LSB of the first CRC byte and the CRC LSB in the MSB of the last, so the CRC goes out MSB first as V.42 8.1.2.3 requires.
notes: Figure C-5.

requirement: Reference algorithm: process each byte LSB first with a right-shifting register XORed with 0x9299 (bit-reversed polynomial, x^16 implied), initial value 0, no final XOR.
Code Example C-1 may be used to compute the header CRC byte by byte.
With the reference algorithm, send the least significant byte of the computed CRC first, then the most significant.
The receiver extracts the two CRC bytes and reassembles them in the correct order before comparing.

notes: Unnumbered shall.

GAP: the RESET FRAME ID modulus is only 'appropriate modulo'. Reading: modulo 256, the size of its 8-bit field in both types 3 and 12.

CONFLICT: the RESET RX WIN CMND rules disagree on direction: the sender puts its own TX-LWE in NEW RECEIVE LWE (p.C-38), but the receiver is told to set its TX LWE from it (p.C-39), while the field name and the flag's definition point to the receiver's RX LWE. Settled by the worked two-node scenario dts-arq/rx-win-cmnd-sets-rx-lwe: the receiver of RESET RX WIN CMND sets its RX LWE (not its TX LWE) to NEW RECEIVE LWE, then sends RESET ACK. Three statements agree on this (the flag aligns the sender's TX LWE with the receiver's RX LWE, C-0262; the sender sends its TX LWE, C-0263; NEW RECEIVE LWE is the new receiver RX LWE, C-0269) against one (C-0265). Worked case: B sends data to A; B's TX LWE is 5 while A's RX LWE is 1, so B's TX WIN LWE flag fails Test 2 at A. B commands NEW RECEIVE LWE 5. Read as printed, A's RX LWE stays 1, Test 2 still fails, and A's own TX LWE jumps to 5 though B never received a D_PDU from A: the command fixes nothing and breaks the other direction. Read as settled, A's RX LWE becomes 5 and B's next D_PDU is in sync. Our transmit window is never changed by the command (C-1178)

requirement: No particular state machine implementation is mandated; interoperability requires behaviour consistent with the state transition and action rules and message formats given here

DTS states, transitions and actions are defined and kept per specified remote node address
Actions and transitions are driven only by PDUs addressed to this node from the remote node whose state is kept, never by PDUs to other nodes or from other nodes
notes: Addressed includes multicast addresses this node belongs to (C.7.5.2.1, p.C-112)

requirement: Actions and transitions are driven only by D_Primitives that reference the remote node whose state is kept

requirement: The DTS meets the flow-control requirements a to p below
Each node keeps a transmit and a receive flow-control window for each connection
Frame sequence numbers are assigned uniquely and sequentially, ascending modulo 256 or 65,536, as the C_PDU is segmented into D_PDUs
A frame sequence number is not reused for another D_PDU until the receiver has acknowledged the D_PDU it was given to
TX LWE is the lowest-numbered outstanding unacknowledged D_PDU, in modulo terms
TX UWE is the number of the last new D_PDU transmitted (highest, in modulo terms)
The current transmitter window size is the modulo difference between TX UWE and (TX LWE minus 1)

requirement: RX LWE is the oldest (lowest, in modulo terms) D_PDU number not yet received

requirement: Greater than, "less than" and the inequalities of Equations 1 to 5 are on the circular sequence space. One special case: in Equation 5, when nothing is outstanding (TX UWE = TX LWE - 1) no acknowledged FSN is in sync. Equations 1 to 4 use their arcs as written, including at the initial values (for example Equation 1 at start-up accepts TX UWE from RX UWE = M - 1 forward to RX LWE + MAX WIN SIZE - 1). reason: Non-ARQ with errors not in profile (main Table 2; plan 4.3)

requirement: Senders always set NOT USED bits to zero; the standard does not say what a receiver does with a set NOT USED bit (NOT STATED). Reading: the receiver ignores them and processes the D_PDU normally.
notes: Coordinator ruling 2026-11-07; corpus keeps such bytes out of byte-exact cases. Exercised by corpus dts-nonarq-management-ack (type 6 byte 4+m NOT USED bits set).

requirement: For a D_PDU type undefined in Ed3 (received from or framed for an Ed3 peer), the minimum header size used to bound parsing is 6 bytes (4 fixed bytes plus the 2-byte header CRC, address excluded).
notes: Coordinator ruling 2026-11-07; used by the corpus error cases.

source: Ed4 C.4.5 (ACK-ONLY, Fig C-12); JITC TP p.135
requirement: The JITC test bytes that inject an undefined type 10 under Ed1 are read under Ed4 as an ACK-ONLY with a header size below the minimum for that type (Figure C-12), so an Ed4 receiver treats them as an invalid D_PDU; the JITC expectation of WARNING for an unknown type holds only for an Ed3-peer reading.
notes: Corpus cases jitc-type10 (Ed3-peer) and its Ed4 bad_header_size twin.

requirement: A sender sets EXTENDED MESSAGE to match whether extended bytes are present (C-0303, C-0304); what a receiver does when the flag and the header size disagree is NOT STATED. Reading: the flag is carried as received and the extended bytes are those the header size gives; no error is raised.
notes: Coordinator ruling 2026-11-07. Corpus cases dpdu-t6-flag-set-no-data and dpdu-t6-flag-clear-with-data.

requirement: How a received EOT becomes an end time, and how several are combined, is NOT STATED. Reading: each valid header with EOT > 0 gives t_rx + EOT x 500 ms, where t_rx is the time the bytes completing that header arrived, or the burst end for a header found only by the search at the burst end (C-1025) (EOT 0 gives none, C-0105). Each is an upper bound on the true end (EOT rounds up and the bytes arrive after the D_PDU started), so the estimate of a burst is the earliest of its end times. A new burst does not clear the estimate of an earlier one: the later of the two is used, since the node may not transmit before either (C-0844).
notes: core-architecture.md section 10 item 2. The estimate overstates the end by at least the receive latency of one block; that costs turnaround, never safety (T4 measures it). Corpus scenarios dts-rx-*. Taking the earliest rather than the latest end time of a burst is what 'as accurately as possible' asks: with a long interleaver the end times of one compliant transmission can differ by about one interleaver block plus 0.5 s, and every one of them is still at or after the real end. A tighter bound than t_rx would need the modem's decoding delay, which the core does not know.

requirement: How the receiver searches the modem output for D_PDUs, and where it resumes after a failure, is NOT STATED. Reading: the bytes of one modem burst are one stream, searched bytewise for the sync 90 EB across block boundaries. A candidate whose header fails a check (size fields, header CRC) is not a D_PDU and the search moves on by one byte. A candidate that needs more bytes waits for the next block; at the burst end the waiting stops, the search continues over what is left, and a partial D_PDU is dropped. A valid header is acted on (EOT, addresses) as soon as it is complete, before its data arrives.
notes: The modem port delivers whole bytes (plan 5.1), so the bit-level alignment search of C-0973 and D-0007 reduces to a byte search (D-0016). Moving on by one byte, not by the claimed header length, means a false sync cannot hide a real D_PDU that starts inside it. EXTENSION resumes after its header CRC (C-0365).

requirement: NOT STATED: the first C_PDU ID NUMBER a node uses. Reading: the type 7 and the type 8 counters each start at 0 when the node starts and go up by one, modulo 4096, for each C_PDU as it is segmented, which is when a transmission first places it
notes: C-0326, C-0328, C-0359; core-architecture.md 5.2 (segmented at build time)

requirement: NOT STATED: the order in which a transmission is filled across kinds of D_PDU. Reading: MANAGEMENT, then WARNING, then CAS-1 control C_PDUs, then expedited traffic, then ACK-ONLY, then retransmissions, then first transmissions of data by priority then age, then non-ARQ repeats, then fill. A data item that does not fit stops its class, so lower priority never overtakes; an item of another class that does not fit is skipped
notes: core-architecture.md 5.3 and section 10 item 7; C-0855, C-0297, C-0288, C-0851, C-0853, B-0280

requirement: A configured maximum transmission length must never block one D_PDU, but how far a transmission may then exceed it is NOT STATED. Reading: when the first D_PDU the build would take does not fit within the configured length, the transmission is made exactly the whole modem blocks that D_PDU needs; other D_PDUs may use what is left of those blocks, and nothing else lengthens it. A D_PDU that needs more than 127.5 s on the waveform in use cannot be sent, which is a configuration error
notes: C-0551, C-0878, K-0094, K-0095; refines core-architecture.md 5.3, which let other D_PDUs fill up to 127.5 s

requirement: EOT counts from the start of the D_PDU, but where a D_PDU starts on air inside an interleaved modem block is NOT STATED. Reading: a D_PDU starts on air at the start of the block holding its first byte (preamble plus whole blocks before it), the earliest instant any of its bits is sent, so its EOT and reception window are never early
notes: C-0104, C-0350, C-0891, D-0017; core-architecture.md 5.6 and section 10 item 4

requirement: A non-ARQ request in EXPEDITED-DATA(UNCONNECTED) waits until the expedited transmission completes (C-0615, C-0737), but when that is reached is NOT STATED. Reading: a type 7 C_PDU is not placed in a transmission while an expedited C_PDU to the same destination is still waiting to be placed; it may go in the same transmission after the last of them
notes: C-0615, C-0737, C-0288. Per destination because the unconnected DTS state is kept per peer (C-0565 to C-0568; core-architecture.md 4.2); Table C-13 itself says all expedited data

requirement: The rejection of a C_PDU dropped for TTL is worded for any C_PDU but sits in the ARQ paragraph, and for non-ARQ the text says only that queued D_PDUs of expired C_PDUs are dropped; how the DTS notices a TTD passing is NOT STATED. Reading: a queued non-ARQ C_PDU whose TTD is at or before now is dropped whole, including copies still owed after some were sent, and rejected to the CAS with D_UNIDATA_REQUEST_REJECTED reason TTL expired; the CAS passes C_UNIDATA_REQUEST_REJECTED to the SIS, which answers its client only if confirmation was asked. One timer, dts.ttd, runs to the earliest TTD in the transmit queue (started or restarted when that changes, cancelled when the queue empties), and the check is repeated on entry to LINKING. A request whose TTD has already passed when it reaches the DTS is rejected at once. Expedited requests carry no TTD and never expire
notes: C-0857, C-0859, C-0864, A-0105, A-0232; core-architecture.md 3.2 (collapsing rule), 3.5 rule 4, 5.3

requirement: The reception window must cover the remaining time during which parts of the C_PDU may arrive, but its value when copies remain for later transmissions is NOT STATED. Reading: window = ceil((planned end of this transmission - start of the D_PDU's block + n x X) / 500), at most 65535, where n is the number of further transmissions the copies still owed need (first copies of unsent segments, then repeats round by round, packed in that order into transmissions of the configured length, a copy longer than that going alone) and X = min(127500, dts.max_transmission_ms) + the LBT wait after an own transmission (lbt_wait_vdcd_ms; lbt_wait_dcd_ms in ed3 mode) + num_cont_slots x cont_slot_width_ms. With nothing owed afterwards, n = 0 and the window equals the EOT
notes: C-0350, C-0352, C-0884, K-0074, K-0107, C-1043; core-architecture.md 5.6 and section 10 item 5, here with n made exact

requirement: The sender must not send segments of a C_PDU after its reception window has expired, but how it decides is NOT STATED. Reading: copies still owed for a C_PDU are placed only in a transmission whose longest possible length (preamble, the whole blocks of its capacity, flush) ends by the earliest window end stamped on that C_PDU in the last transmission that carried it; otherwise every copy still owed is dropped, with no rejection (its TTL has not expired, and non-ARQ has no confirmation). Checked on entry to LINKING
notes: C-0353, C-1051; core-architecture.md 5.6 (the window is a commitment). T3 (P3-7): the check does not allow for host latency (transmit output to transmit_done beyond the planned duration). The slack is the unused part of the num_cont_slots allowance of C-1051, the whole-block remainder and the half-second rounding. Jitter, ed3 and slotted below the last position always leave at least one slot spare, so no drops at 0 to 300 ms; slotted at the last position (K-0082) can have zero slack, so any latency drops the last repeat of each U_PDU

requirement: A C_PDU ID is not reused until the reception window of the C_PDU that had it has expired, and IDs go up by one (C-1040), but what happens when the next ID is still in use is NOT STATED. Reading: an ID is held until the latest window end announced for its C_PDU (an ID given in the transmission being built counts as in use); a C_PDU that would need a held ID is not placed, which stops its class, and while one waits the dts.ttd timer also runs to the instant the ID is freed, so the queue is looked at again then

Repeated D_PDUs should be spread across a transmission to ride out long fades, but the placement is NOT STATED. Reading: selection takes the owed copies C_PDU by C_PDU, by priority then age, and within a C_PDU lowest copy number first, then segment order; a copy that does not fit stops the class. Layout puts the first copies of the transmission first, in the order chosen, then each round of repeats (every copy numbered 2, then every copy numbered 3, and so on, the number counting every transmission of that D_PDU so far), each round in the order chosen. When the repeated D_PDUs share one count, this puts a whole round between the copies of each D_PDU. This replaces the insertion formula of core-architecture.md 5.3, which puts the copies of each segment of a multi-segment C_PDU next to each other
notes: C-0885, C-0884, C-0848; core-architecture.md 5.3 (P3-5 departure)

requirement: MANAGEMENT(UNCONNECTED) holds non-ARQ requests until the management protocol has completed (C-0635, C-0636), but when the receiving side of the type 6 exchange completes is NOT STATED. Reading: for a node that received a MANAGEMENT D_PDU, the exchange is complete once its acknowledgement is placed in a transmission; non-ARQ D_PDUs to that peer may follow the acknowledgement in the same transmission, and the peer then leaves MANAGEMENT(UNCONNECTED) by C-0738. Because MANAGEMENT D_PDUs go first in every transmission (C-0297, C-1041), no request is ever held behind one.
notes: C-0635, C-0636, C-0738, C-0297, C-0744; corpus dts-nonarq-management-ack

requirement: C-0920 refuses an Ed3 data rate or frequency change MANAGEMENT D_PDU 'from an Ed3 peer', but before CAS-1 negotiation a sender's edition is unknown (NOT STATED how to tell). Reading: the EOW names the procedure. A type 6 with VALID MESSAGE set carrying EOW type 1, 2, 5 or 6 (C-0919) is acknowledged and, when new (not a repeat by frame ID), refused with WARNING reason 3 (C-0921), whatever edition is recorded for the sender; nothing in it is acted on. Types 2, 5 and 6 are also unrecognised EOWs (C-0421), so they also get an UNRECOGNIZED-TYPE-ERROR (C-0445). The J-0054 WARNING reason 0 is left for the other unrecognised EOWs in a type 6 (7 and 14); 13 draws reason 3 (J-0081).
notes: C-0919, C-0920, C-0921, C-0421, C-0445, J-0054; corpus dts-nonarq-management-repeat-same-id, dts-nonarq-management-ed3-drc-warning-3. J-0054 reason 0 is P5-3 (mac/type6-unknown-subtype) Delivered by P5-3 as J-0081 (mac/type6-unknown-subtype; EOW 13 draws reason 3, mac/type6-token-eow-warning-3).

requirement: C-0296 requires every received MANAGEMENT D_PDU to be acknowledged, while C-0302 says one with VALID MESSAGE 0 is used only as an acknowledgement; acknowledging those would make two nodes acknowledge each other for ever (NOT STATED). Reading: a type 6 with VALID MESSAGE 0 is an acknowledgement only. It is not acknowledged and is not compared with RX MANAGEMENT FRAME ID NUMBER; its ACK flag is matched only against a MANAGEMENT message this node sent, and is ignored when none is outstanding.
notes: C-0296, C-0302, C-0314; this node sends no MANAGEMENT message before phase 7

requirement: The MANAGEMENT FRAME ID NUMBER of an acknowledgement is NOT STATED. Reading: the acknowledgement carries the frame ID of the type 6 it acknowledges, so the sender can match it; TX MANAGEMENT FRAME ID NUMBER is neither used nor advanced, since it numbers management messages (C-0311, C-0317) and an acknowledgement carries none. The acknowledgement has VALID MESSAGE 0, EXTENDED MESSAGE 0, no extended bytes, and EOW EMPTY unless one is owed to that peer (C-1079).
notes: C-0296, C-0302, C-0304, C-0311, C-0312, C-0317; corpus dts-nonarq-management-ack

requirement: How many acknowledgements answer repeated copies of a MANAGEMENT D_PDU is NOT STATED (C-0295 recommends repeating). Reading: a copy that arrives while an acknowledgement of the same frame ID to that peer is still queued and unsent adds nothing; a copy that arrives after the acknowledgement was sent is acknowledged again, since the first may have been lost (C-0296). Only a new frame ID is acted on (C-0315, C-0316).
notes: C-0295, C-0296, C-0315, C-0316, C-1016; corpus dts-nonarq-management-repeat-same-id

requirement: How many WARNINGs a burst of offending D_PDUs draws, and when the CAS is told D_WARNING_TRANSMITTED, are NOT STATED. Reading: a WARNING already queued and unsent to the same peer with the same RECEIVED FRAME TYPE and reason is not queued again, so a run of segments draws one; the CAS is told D_WARNING_TRANSMITTED when the WARNING is queued, because no primitive may be produced while the MAC builds a transmission (core-architecture.md 3.5 rule 4).
notes: C-0376, C-0578, C-0733; corpus dts-nonarq-warning-reason-1-arq-while-unconnected

requirement: Non-ARQ reassembly uses the C_PDU ID, offset and sizes (C-0531), but what identifies a C_PDU across senders, and what to do with a segment that does not fit, are NOT STATED. Reading: a C_PDU is keyed by (source address, destination address with its group flag, type 7 or 8, C_PDU ID), the two types being separate ID spaces (C-0328, C-0359); the destination is in the key because C-0326 does not say whether a sender numbers C_PDUs across all destinations or per destination, and every segment of one C_PDU carries the same destination, so keying by it never splits a C_PDU. A segment whose offset plus size exceeds the C_PDU size it states is discarded. A segment whose stated C_PDU size differs from the C_PDU held under its key starts a new C_PDU in place of the held one: the sender may reuse an ID once its window has passed (C-0327), and our deadline is later than its window (C-1077).

A receiver can use the reception window to release a partial C_PDU (C-0354), but how it turns the window into a deadline is NOT STATED. Reading: a segment's deadline is the time of the bytes_received that completed its D_PDU plus its C_PDU RECEPTION WINDOW in half seconds; that is never earlier than the sender meant, since the window counts from the D_PDU's start (C-0350), as with EOT (C-1024). A C_PDU's deadline is the latest of its segments'. An incomplete C_PDU is discarded at its deadline (C-0336), a deadline at or before now counting as passed. The deadlines of incomplete C_PDUs share one timer, dts.reception_window, run at the earliest (core-architecture.md 3.2).
notes: C-0336, C-0350, C-0354, C-1024; corpus dts-nonarq-rx-two-segments-out-of-order, dts-nonarq-rx-window-expires

requirement: What a receiver does with further copies of a non-ARQ C_PDU it has already delivered (a sender's repeats, A-0081, C-0884) is NOT STATED. Reading: delivering a C_PDU leaves a record of its key, size and deadline; a later segment with the same key and C_PDU size before that deadline is a copy and is dropped, and extends the deadline to its own if later. The record has no timer: it is stale once its deadline is at or before now, and is replaced by the next C_PDU with that key, which C-0327 makes a new C_PDU.
notes: C-0327, C-0539, A-0081, C-0884; corpus dts-nonarq-rx-copy-not-delivered-twice

requirement: A node should answer an unrecognised EOW with UNRECOGNIZED-TYPE-ERROR (C-0445), but which D_PDU carries it, and which received EOWs count, are NOT STATED. Reading: only an EOW in a D_PDU addressed to this node's individual address is answered (as for WARNINGs, C-0394); the answer goes in the EOW field of the next D_PDU placed for that peer's individual address, of any type (C-0396), replacing EMPTY; a later answer still unsent replaces an earlier one; nothing is sent only to carry it. Unrecognised types are 2, 5, 6, 7 and 14 (C-0405, C-0412, C-0421); 13 was in this list until P5-3 (J-0081). UNRECOGNIZED-TYPE-ERROR is an All-editions EOW (C-0401, C-0415), so it may go to a peer of unknown edition.
notes: C-0396, C-0401, C-0415, C-0421, C-0445; corpus dts-nonarq-eow-unrecognised-type-3, dts-nonarq-management-ed3-drc-warning-3 P5-3: EOW 13 is taken out of the unrecognised list (J-0070, J-0081).

requirement: When the DTS confirms an expedited non-ARQ request is NOT STATED (non-ARQ has no acknowledgement). Reading: D_EXPEDITED_UNIDATA_REQUEST_CONFIRM is sent when the transmission carrying the last D_PDU of the C_PDU ends (transmit_done); it is how the CAS learns that its CAS-1 C_PDU has been sent (B-0400)
notes: Normal non-ARQ requests are not confirmed before P6-1

requirement: GAP: when to retransmit D_PDUs that no acknowledgement ever answers, and after how long, is NOT STATED; the node may retransmit or not (C-0911). Reading: a per-peer wait, dts.ack_wait/<peer>, with the configurable dts.ack_wait_ms, is started or restarted when a transmission that carried ARQ data D_PDUs to the peer ends and some of them await acknowledgement, peers in ascending address order; it stops when an acknowledgement from the peer leaves none awaiting, or when the connection ends; at expiry every D_PDU still awaiting acknowledgement is taken to have failed and is retransmitted (the retransmit strategy of C-0911). With dts.ack_wait_ms unset the wait is derived, so a node always has one: the longest a peer that heard us and shares our settings takes to answer, the longer LBT wait (it may have heard only part of our transmission, K-0077) plus the longest contention wait plus a transmission of the configured length. An explicit value shorter than the peer's LBT wait can make a sender retransmit again and again before a peer that heard it only in part may answer
notes: core-architecture.md 10 item 6; plan A4 (T4 to recommend a value)

requirement: The half duplex recommendation (C-0910) is adopted. Reading: on every ACK-ONLY or DATA-ACK from the peer, a D_PDU awaiting acknowledgement fails if a clear bit covers it (C-0908), if it is at the RX LWE carried (C-0776), or if it lies after the last D_PDU this acknowledgement explicitly acknowledges by a set bit or, with no set bit, after RX LWE - 1 (C-0910). No allowance for early turnaround is needed: this node never transmits before the incoming transmission has ended (C-0844)

GAP: when TX WIN UWE and TX WIN LWE are judged for a D_PDU sent in a transmission that also carries later new D_PDUs is NOT STATED. Reading: with the window as it stands once every FSN of the transmission has been allocated, so TX WIN UWE marks only the last new D_PDU of the transmission; retransmissions are judged afresh each time they are sent

GAP: a receiver cannot tell whether a D_PDU it has not received belonged to a C_PDU sent with DELIVER IN ORDER. Reading of C-0178: a complete C_PDU with DELIVER IN ORDER is delivered once every D_PDU before its first segment has been received (RX LWE has passed its last segment); several so released go in FSN order. A C_PDU without the flag is delivered when complete (C-0179)

GAP: the DROP method (C-0860, C-0862) does not say what happens to segments that never had an FSN, or which flags a DROP PDU carries. Reading: when the TTD of an ARQ C_PDU passes it is rejected at once (C-0859); if no segment has an FSN it is simply removed; otherwise every segment not yet acknowledged goes as a DROP PDU, retransmitted when it fails, and every segment never sent goes too, as a new D_PDU, so the receiver sees the whole C_PDU end (C-0862). A DROP PDU keeps the C_PDU START and C_PDU END of its segment, carries no segment and SIZE 0 (C-0182, C-0183), and is sent like any other ARQ D_PDU (window, retransmission)

CONFLICT: a DROP PDU is acknowledged whatever its data CRC (C-0204, C-0217), but D_PDUs with a failed data CRC are discarded before the state machine (C-0836). Reading: the DROP PDU is the exception and reaches the state machine. A C_PDU whose run of segments from C_PDU START to C_PDU END includes a DROP PDU is discarded when the run is complete, whichever segment carried the flag and in whatever order they arrived (C-0184)

GAP: whether a received copy of a D_PDU behind RX LWE is acknowledged. Reading: it is not stored, delivered or allowed to move the edges back (C-0777), but it owes an acknowledgement, which carries RX LWE back to a sender that lost the earlier one (the tables say acknowledge every DATA-ONLY, C-0658). With the 16-bit window of half the circle every FSN not within the window ahead of RX LWE lies behind it; no acknowledgement covers such an FSN by itself (C-0779)

GAP: how the ordering rules C-0850 and C-0851 meet a full transmit window. Reading: an ARQ C_PDU with no segment sent whose peer window is full (or which waits for expedited data, C-1131) is passed over and later data may go; an ARQ C_PDU with some segments sent goes first among first transmissions (C-0850 over C-0851) and, if its next segment cannot be placed for any reason, no other first transmission of data is placed in that transmission, so nothing splits its segments
notes: C-0855 still lets non-data D_PDUs sit between them

source: Ed4 C.4.5; C.4.6; Tables C-18, C-20
requirement: GAP: how acknowledgements are generated is left to the implementation (C-0215, C-0658 as appropriate). Reading: a DATA-ONLY or DATA-ACK processed from a peer owes it one acknowledgement; each transmission carries at most one ACK-ONLY per peer owed one (C-0370), in peer address order after the expedited D_PDUs, built at placement from the receive window then: RX LWE, encoding 0 (bitmap), offset 0, the bitmap from RX LWE + 1 to RX UWE. When a data D_PDU to the same peer goes in the same transmission and the bitmap fits in 18 bytes, the first one becomes a DATA-ACK carrying it and the ACK-ONLY is dropped (C-0238, C-0249). Repeats, run length encoding, offsets and splitting are P4-3s
notes: core-architecture.md 10 item 15. Refined by C-1150 to C-1152 and C-1154 (P4-3): encodings, offsets, the merge rule and repeats in fill

requirement: Reading for P4-2 ahead of P4-6: DATA-ONLY, ACK-ONLY and DATA-ACK from a peer connected with the 16-bit family are processed the same way in all four CONNECTED states, since Tables C-22 and C-24 give the same processing as C-20 (C-0698 to C-0700, C-0718 to C-0720). Their send-side limits (ACK-ONLY rather than DATA-ACK, no new data, an ACK-ONLY deferred until the management exchange ends) are met by the planner class order: the management acknowledgement and any expedited D_PDU are placed before ARQ data in the same transmission, which ends those states (C-1070, C-0738, C-1131)
notes: P4-6 owns the EXPEDITED-DATA(CONNECTED) and MANAGEMENT(CONNECTED) rows

requirement: GAP: when D_UNIDATA_REQUEST_CONFIRM is sent (as appropriate). Reading: when every segment of the C_PDU has been acknowledged by the peer; C_PDUs completed by one acknowledgement are confirmed in arrival order. A C_PDU rejected for its TTD (C-0859, C-1124) is never confirmed

Reading: ARQ data D_PDUs to a peer, first transmissions and retransmissions, are not placed while an expedited C_PDU to the same peer has unplaced segments, as C-1044 does for type 7: in EXPEDITED-DATA(CONNECTED) ARQ requests wait for the expedited data (C-0693) and types 9 and 11 are not among the types that state sends (C-0747)

Reading: failed D_PDUs are retransmitted ahead of every first transmission of data (C-0852, C-0905), highest priority first, then by the age of their C_PDU, then in FSN order (C-0853); a retransmission that does not fit is passed over for the next. Each keeps its FSN and segment; it may become a DATA-ACK when it is the first data D_PDU to its peer in the transmission (C-1128)

CONFLICT: a D_PDU whose data CRC fails is discarded (C-0836, C-0839), but a header with a good CRC is processed whatever the data CRC (C-0141), and the acknowledgement of a DATA-ACK lies wholly in its header so that it stays usable when the data is corrupt (C.4.6.3). Reading: a DATA-ACK (type 11) from a peer with a 16-bit ARQ machine whose data CRC fails has its acknowledgement part (RX LWE and Selective Acks) processed as an ACK-ONLY's would be, with the state change a DATA-ACK makes; its segment is discarded, not stored and not acknowledged (C-0216). Otherwise C-0839 stands: with no ARQ machine for the peer it is discarded. The 8-bit type 2 is P4-5's

GAP: a sender may use either Ack Data encoding and should send the more compact (C-0224, C-0225), but which run length codes make up an encoding, and the choice on a tie, are NOT STATED. Reading: the acknowledged bits are the receive window from RX LWE + 1 (plus 256 x Offset) upwards, ending at RX UWE (C-0207 to C-0209, C-0233). Run length encoding takes each run of equal bits in turn and codes it in the fewest bytes: a one-byte code for a run of up to 64 bits, a two-byte code for a run of 65 to 16384 bits, and a longer run as two-byte codes of 16384 bits each followed by one code for the rest. The bitmap is zero padded to a whole byte. The shorter of the two is sent; on a tie, the bitmap (encoding 0). The same choice applies to the Selective Acks of a DATA-ACK
notes: C-0224, C-0225, C-0227 to C-0232, C-0246, C-0247; corpus dts-arq-ack-rle-long-run, dts-arq-ack-long-form-crc

requirement: GAP: acknowledgements may be spread over several ACK-ONLY D_PDUs with different offsets (C-0212, C-0222), together they must acknowledge everything received (C-0215), and each ACK-ONLY should be kept small (C-0213), but how small and how a window is split are NOT STATED beyond the annex noting that the offset lets the Ack Data stay within 32 bytes [Ed4 C.4.5.5, p.C-31]. Reading: the Ack Data of each ACK-ONLY is at most 32 bytes, so it is in the header form when it is 21 bytes or fewer (C-0218) and otherwise in the long form (C-0219). When neither encoding of the whole window fits 32 bytes, the window is cut at multiples of 256 FSNs: the first ACK-ONLY, at Offset 0, covers the largest whole number of 256-FSN units whose more compact encoding (C-1150) fits in 32 bytes (at least one, since one unit is a 32-byte bitmap), and each following one starts at the Offset where the previous ended, the last covering the rest up to RX UWE. All carry the same RX LWE. They are placed in one transmission, in Offset order, all or none: if together they do not fit, none is placed and the acknowledgement stays owed. A window that fits is acknowledged by one ACK-ONLY at Offset 0. The fill repeats these small ACK-ONLY D_PDUs (C-0214, C-1154)
notes: C-0212, C-0213, C-0215, C-0218, C-0219, C-0221 to C-0223, C-0233; refines C-1128; corpus dts-arq-ack-offset; coordinator ruling on P4-3

requirement: Reading, refining C-1128 for the encodings: the acknowledgement owed to a peer is merged into the first data D_PDU to it in the transmission, as a DATA-ACK, only when it is a single ACK-ONLY (Offset 0, C-0250) whose Ack Data, in the encoding chosen by C-1150, is at most 18 bytes (C-0248); the DATA-ACK then carries that encoding bit and those bytes as its Selective Acks (C-0246, C-0247). Otherwise every ACK-ONLY of the acknowledgement is sent and the data goes as DATA-ONLY (C-0249). The acknowledgement a DATA-ACK carries is also repeated as an ACK-ONLY in the fill (C-0240, C-1154)
notes: C-0238, C-0240, C-0246 to C-0250, C-1128; corpus dts-arq-data-ack-merge

requirement: GAP: a receiver supports both Ack Data encodings (C-0226), but what it does with run length codes that do not end cleanly or that reach beyond the window is NOT STATED. Reading: the Ack Data is decoded into bits from FSN RX LWE + 1 + 256 x Offset (C-0233; Offset 0 for a DATA-ACK, C-0250): eight per bitmap byte, padding included, or the Length + 1 bits of each run length code in turn; a two-byte code cut short by the end of the field adds nothing; bits for FSNs 32768 or more ahead of RX LWE are ignored, since no D_PDU can be outstanding there (C-0779). The bits are then used as a bitmap's are (C-0202, C-0205, C-1121): the half duplex rule of C-1121 is applied for each ACK-ONLY on its own, so after a set of ACK-ONLY D_PDUs with different offsets every D_PDU acknowledged by any of them is acknowledged and the rest have failed

GAP: spare space in a transmission of whole modem blocks should be filled (C-0886, C-0887), with repeated ACK-ONLY D_PDUs and PADDING D_PDUs, PADDING only towards Ed4 peers (C-0367), but the order, amount and addressing are NOT STATED. Reading: after the chosen D_PDUs are laid out, the spare bytes of the last block they need are filled, never adding a block: first with copies of every acknowledgement of the transmission as ACK-ONLY D_PDUs (an acknowledgement carried by a DATA-ACK included, C-0240), taken in turn in the order they stand in the transmission, stopping at the first copy that does not fit (C-0214, C-0369, C-0882); then, if every addressee of the transmission is an individual address recorded Ed4 by CAS-1 negotiation (B-0408; it stays recorded after a link ends), as many PADDING D_PDUs as fit, addressed to the lowest addressee address, EOW EMPTY unless one is owed to it (C-1079); the rest is left to the modem's zero fill. A peer of unknown edition, an Ed3 peer, or any group or broadcast addressee means no PADDING (C-0055, C-0560). Fill D_PDUs carry EOT like any other (C-0104, C-1043)
notes: C-0055, C-0214, C-0240, C-0367 to C-0370, C-0560, C-0882, C-0886, C-0887, B-0408; core-architecture.md 5.5; corpus dts-tx-fill-ack-repeats, dts-tx-fill-padding-ed4, dts-tx-no-align-ed3-peer, and the fill re-derived in the dts-arq scenarios of P4-2

requirement: GAP: towards Ed4 peers any segment may be short (C-0553) and segment sizes may be chosen so D_PDUs line up with modem blocks (C-0871, C-0872) or fill blocks (C-0887 item 3), but the procedure is NOT STATED. Reading: it is applied only to first transmissions of ARQ data D_PDUs to a peer recorded Ed4 (B-0408). When the next segment at the maximum segment size (or the rest of the C_PDU, if shorter) is cut, its D_PDU's position in the transmission's layout is known: if the D_PDU would run past the transmission's capacity, the segment is cut so the D_PDU ends exactly at the capacity, which is a block boundary; otherwise, if the segment is not the C_PDU's last and its D_PDU would end inside a block after crossing at least one block boundary, the segment is cut so the D_PDU ends at the last boundary it crosses. Either cut is made only if at least one byte of segment is left; otherwise the segment is not shortened. When the capacity was stretched past the configured transmission length only for this D_PDU, as the first of the transmission (C-1042), and the cut leaves it needing fewer blocks, the capacity becomes the larger of the configured length and the blocks it now needs, so nothing else lengthens the transmission. The rest of the C_PDU becomes later segments with the next FSNs. Apart from the capacity cut, a C_PDU's last segment is never shortened; retransmissions (which keep their size, C-0549), DROP PDUs and non-ARQ D_PDUs (types 7 and 8, whose segments are cut once at first placement and copied for repeats, C-0352) are never shortened at all, and towards Ed3 peers, peers of unknown edition and group or broadcast addresses nothing is (C-0554, C-0560, C-0870). Positions are those of the layout when the segment is cut; an ACK-ONLY that a later DATA-ACK to another peer absorbs (C-1152) can move a D_PDU already aligned, which the standard's should (C-0872) tolerates
notes: C-0352, C-0508, C-0549, C-0550, C-0553, C-0554, C-0560, C-0870 to C-0872, C-0887, C-1042; core-architecture.md 5.4; corpus dts-tx-block-align-ed4, dts-tx-no-align-ed3-peer

requirement: GAP: what a node does with a D_PDU that fails one of Tests 1 to 5, and when it starts the procedure of C.7.4. Reading: the D_PDU is not used at all: its data is neither stored, delivered nor acknowledged (so an FSN in the gap Equation 3 leaves out of sync draws no ACK-ONLY, C-0779), and its acknowledgement part does not move the transmit window. The node at once starts a FULL RESET as initiator (C-0791, C-0792), unless a RESET/WIN-RESYNC command of its own to that peer is already awaiting acknowledgement, in which case nothing more is done
notes: Issue #49 item (c): a copy outside the sync window draws no ACK-ONLY

requirement: The synchronisation verification run when a link is re-established (C-0789) is NOT STATED as a separate step. Reading: every new link starts its ARQ machine at the initial window edges (C-0787; we do not revive old ones, C-0788), and Tests 1 to 5 run on every regular-data D_PDU from then on (C-0790), so the verification is those continuous tests; no extra exchange is sent at link set-up

GAP: RESET/WIN-RESYNC is stop-and-wait (C-0255) but no retry timing is given. Reading: dts.reset_wait/<peer> starts when the transmission carrying our command (FULL RESET CMD, or the RESET RX WIN CMND that answers a RESET TX WIN RQST) has ended, with the acknowledgement wait (dts.ack_wait_ms, or its derived value, C-1120), after any dts.ack_wait starts of that transmission_done, peers in ascending address order. At expiry the same D_PDU, same RESET FRAME ID and fields, is queued again. It stops on the RESET ACK, on a FULL RESET that makes our RX WIN CMND stale (C-1175) or when the connection ends. No retry limit: abandoning the link is link failure (C-0739, phase 5)
notes: For P5-1: link failure detection must also cover a reset exchange that never completes, since regular data is suspended while it is pending and an ARQ-progress check alone would never fire.

requirement: GAP: the RESET FRAME ID sequence (C-0272, C-0273) has no start value, and the acknowledgements are not covered. Reading: each connection starts a sequence at 0 on D_CONNECTION_MADE; a command takes the current value and the next command the next value (modulo 256) only once the previous one has been acknowledged. The last ID received starts at none (above 255) on each new connection; a command whose ID equals it is a copy (C-0271): it is acknowledged again but not acted on again, and causes no state change. Acknowledgements carry RESET FRAME ID 0 (C-0817; the RX WIN CMND acknowledgement is read the same way, RESET ACK 1 and every other field 0), and are never acknowledged (C-0820). A second acknowledgement to a peer is not queued while one is already queued and unsent
tests: dts-arq/sync-test-1-fail-full-reset; dts-arq/full-reset-initiator; dts-arq/full-reset-responder; dts-arq/reset-frame-id-repeat-ignored; dts-arq/rx-win-cmnd-sets-rx-lwe; dts-arq/tx-win-rqst-answered; dts-arq/rx-win-cmnd-repeated

requirement: The place of RESET/WIN-RESYNC D_PDUs in a transmission is NOT STATED. Reading: they are DTS control D_PDUs placed after WARNING and before every class of data (core-architecture.md 5.3), oldest first, so a FULL RESET ACK precedes the data that follows the reset in the same transmission and the receiver resets before it reads that data

GAP: C-0257 suspends the sending of regular data during a RESET/WIN-RESYNC exchange but says nothing of receiving, or of commands that cross. Reading: while our command to a peer awaits its RESET ACK, no DATA-ONLY, ACK-ONLY or DATA-ACK is sent to that peer, and those received from it are discarded unused (the windows they would be judged against are about to change); a RESET TX WIN RQST or RESET RX WIN CMND from it is neither acted on nor acknowledged until our exchange ends (one exchange at a time; the peer repeats it); a FULL RESET CMD from it is always acted on. A FULL RESET, in either role, withdraws a pending RX WIN CMND of ours, whose NEW RECEIVE LWE it makes stale; a pending FULL RESET CMD of ours stays pending

source: Ed4 C.7.4; Tables C-18, C-20, C-22
requirement: GAP: "partially completed C_PDUs" (C-0813, C-0823) and the state after a FULL RESET with data still queued. Reading: a C_PDU is partly completed when at least one of its segments has an FSN and it has not been confirmed; those are rejected to the CAS with a local reason (C-0826, C-0866), oldest first, and dts.ack_wait stops; C_PDUs not yet started stay queued. A responder in DATA(CONNECTED) or EXPEDITED-DATA(CONNECTED) goes to IDLE(CONNECTED) (C-0681, C-0701) and then, if ARQ C_PDUs remain queued for the peer, to DATA(CONNECTED), as their arrival would have done (C-0653); otherwise an acknowledgement of the data that follows would draw WARNING reason 3 (C-0659)

GAP: a RESET TX WIN RQST is answered by forcing the resynchronisation with RESET RX WIN CMND (C-0261), and every RESET/WIN-RESYNC received draws a RESET/WIN-RESYNC acknowledgement (C-0256, C-0267). Reading: one D_PDU does both, as C-0268 allows: RESET ACK 1 and RESET RX WIN CMND 1, NEW RECEIVE LWE our TX LWE (C-0263), FULL RESET CMD and RESET TX WIN RQST 0, RESET FRAME ID from our sequence (C-1173). It is our command: regular data to the peer waits for its RESET ACK (C-0257, C-0264) and it is repeated at dts.reset_wait expiry (C-1172). Our transmit window is otherwise unchanged; outstanding D_PDUs stay outstanding

GAP: what happens to the segments a receiver holds when RESET RX WIN CMND moves its RX LWE (read as C-0274 settles it). Reading: a NEW RECEIVE LWE that would pass Test 2 (C-0797), that is, one at or behind RX LWE within the window, changes nothing (the ACK still goes): the sender's TX LWE is already in step, and moving RX LWE back would forget C_PDUs already delivered, so their retransmissions would be delivered twice (C-0777). Otherwise segments held that lie within the maximum window ahead of the new RX LWE are kept, those behind it are discarded; RX UWE becomes the furthest one kept, or NEW RECEIVE LWE - 1; RX LWE then passes every segment already received (C-0776), and in-order C_PDUs now behind RX LWE are delivered, oldest first (C-0178). Keeping them matters: the sender has removed selectively acknowledged D_PDUs from its window and will not send them again. The transmit window is not touched. Then a RESET ACK (C-0266, C-1173)
notes: Review: the Equation 2 guard added so the command never moves RX LWE back over delivered data.

requirement: The handling of RESET/WIN-RESYNC flag combinations is NOT STATED beyond the FULL RESET values (C-0805 to C-0809, C-0816 to C-0818). Reading: RESET ACK is processed first: it ends our pending exchange (and for a FULL RESET CMD of ours, the initiator resets, C-0822 to C-0824); with nothing of ours pending it is ignored. Then FULL RESET CMD 1 is a FULL RESET CMD whatever the other flags; else RESET TX WIN RQST is answered as C-1177 (with RESET RX WIN CMND also set, that answer acknowledges both); else RESET RX WIN CMND is acted on as C-1178. A D_PDU with only RESET ACK, or no flag at all, needs no answer. In MANAGEMENT(CONNECTED) any RESET/WIN-RESYNC draws WARNING reason 3 only (C-0721)

When Tests 1 to 5 are applied relative to the D_PDU's own effect is NOT STATED. Reading: on each DATA-ONLY, ACK-ONLY and DATA-ACK from a peer with a 16-bit ARQ machine, before it changes any window edge: Tests 1 to 3 on the DATA part (including a DATA-ACK whose data CRC failed, since the tested fields are in the checked header, C-1133), Tests 4 and 5 on the acknowledgement part, always with the maximum window size 32768 (C-0796). Equation 5 is applied to the FSNs a bitmap acknowledges (encoding 0, from RX LWE + 1 + 256 x offset); run length encoded acknowledgements (P4-3) are tested on their RX LWE only until P4-3 applies Equation 5 to them. An ACK-ONLY in IDLE(CONNECTED) draws WARNING reason 3 first (C-0659) and is not tested

GAP: how a node acknowledges on a link with the 8-bit family is NOT STATED beyond the field rules: types 1 and 2 carry a SELECTIVE ACKS bitmap of 0 to 16 bytes from RX LWE + 1 (C-0194, C-0201, C-0207, C-0236, C-0245) and have no encoding bit, offset or length field. Reading: the acknowledgement is one bitmap of the whole window from RX LWE + 1 to RX UWE. A sender may have at most 128 D_PDUs outstanding (C-0771) and a receiver accepts nothing beyond RX LWE + 127 (C-0779, C-0798), so the bitmap has at most 127 bits, 16 bytes: it always fits one ED3-ACK-ONLY (no splitting, C-1151 does not apply) and always fits a DATA-ACK, so it merges into the first ARQ data D_PDU to the peer as for the 16-bit family (C-1128, C-1152), and the fill repeats it as an ED3-ACK-ONLY (C-1154). A received type 1 or 2 is read as a bitmap at offset 0 and processed as a type 10 or 11 is (C-1121, C-1153)

GAP: whether the Ed4-only sending options (PADDING, C-0367; short non-final segments, C-0553; modem block alignment, C-0871) apply on a link between Ed4 peers that negotiated Short, and so uses the Ed3 D_PDU family (C-0052, C-0168, B-0232), is NOT STATED. Reading: they follow the peer's edition, not the D_PDU family. Short chooses the D_PDU family only; the peer is still known to be Ed4 (B-0408), and C-0367, C-0553 and C-0871 are worded by the peer's edition. So towards an Ed4 peer on a Short link PADDING fills spare space and ARQ segments are aligned with modem blocks as on a 16-bit link (C-1154, C-1155); towards an Ed3 peer neither is used (C-0367, C-0554, C-0870)

GAP: what a node does with a regular ARQ D_PDU of the family its link does not use (types 9 to 12 on a link negotiated Short, types 0 to 3 on a 16-bit link) is NOT STATED; the families are never mixed on one link (C-0763). Reading: the D_PDU is recognised but not allowed in the connection's current state, so it is not processed (no data stored, delivered or acknowledged, no window edge moved, no state change) and draws WARNING reason 3 (C-0391, C-0382) with D_WARNING_TRANSMITTED to the CAS (C-0733). From a peer recorded Ed3, types 9 to 12 are undefined and draw reason 0 instead (C-0388). EXPEDITED-DATA and EXPEDITED-ACK (types 4 and 5) belong to both families and are not affected

GAP: dts.max_window is one node setting (C-0772), but the maximum window size differs by family, 128 or 32,768 (C-0771), and the maximum allowable window may not exceed it (C-0773). Reading: on each link the maximum allowable window is the smaller of dts.max_window and its family's maximum window size, so the default of 32,768 gives 128 on a link with the 8-bit family. dts.max_window is still checked against 32,768 only

GAP: segments of one C_PDU take consecutive FSNs and are joined in modulo order from C_PDU START to C_PDU END (C-0510, C-0516), but nothing bounds the number of segments by the window or the modulus, and on a link with the 8-bit family a C_PDU of more than 128 segments is ordinary (dts.max_segment_size is a free setting, C-0503); how a receiver tells a held segment from a later one with the same FSN is NOT STATED. Reading: segments are numbered without wrapping in the order RX LWE reaches them; the segments of a C_PDU not yet complete that RX LWE has passed are held for it, and an FSN ahead of RX LWE (within the maximum window, C-0779) is always a new D_PDU, never one of those. A C_PDU of any number of segments is reassembled and delivered once
notes: P4-5 review

requirement: How a receiver keeps the expedited ARQ receive window is NOT STATED: the sender restarts its expedited FSNs at 0 for each C_PDU and numbers C_PDUs modulo 16 (C-0756 to C-0759), and type 5 is laid out as type 1 (C-0291). Reading: one reassembly at a time. A type 4 whose C_PDU ID is neither the one being reassembled nor the one last delivered starts a new reassembly and discards any partial one. RX LWE is the lowest FSN of the current C_PDU not yet received, RX UWE the highest received, and the SELECTIVE ACKS bitmap covers RX LWE + 1 to RX UWE as for type 1; an FSN more than 128 past RX LWE, beyond what 16 bitmap bytes cover, is not stored. The C_PDU is complete when FSN 0, carrying C_PDU START, through an FSN carrying C_PDU END are all held, and is delivered at once with D_EXPEDITED_UNIDATA_INDICATION (ARQ), since type 4 has no DELIVER IN ORDER flag. RX LWE then stays one past its last FSN, and a copy of that C_PDU is acknowledged again but not delivered again. Every type 4 received owes the peer a type 5; one is queued per peer and built from the receive state when it is placed

Where EXPEDITED-ACK-ONLY (type 5) goes in a transmission, and whether the fill repeats it, is NOT STATED. Reading: it is a DTS control D_PDU placed after RESET/WIN-RESYNC and ahead of all client data, expedited type 8 included, so it is never behind DATA-ONLY or DATA-ACK (C-0288). The fill repeats ACK-ONLY D_PDUs only (C-0882, C-1154), not type 5
notes: P4-6. Refines the Expedited class of core-architecture.md 5.3

source: Ed4 C.7.1, Tables C-18 to C-24; C.7.1.3
requirement: Refines C-0738 for the receive side of EXPEDITED-DATA(CONNECTED), whose exit the tables never give. Reading: the expedited exchange is open while a type 5 to the peer is owed and not yet placed, or a type 4 C_PDU from it is partly reassembled (the peer has not finished sending it); a received type 8 owes nothing and holds no state, and a type 8 reassembly does not count. When the exchange closes (on placing the type 5, or at once after a type 5 or type 8 received with nothing open) the node leaves for DATA(CONNECTED) if regular ARQ D_PDUs have flowed on the connection or ARQ or type 7 C_PDUs are queued for the peer, which the end of the exchange releases as if just requested (C-0737, C-0693, C-0695), and otherwise for IDLE(CONNECTED). The same target applies when MANAGEMENT(CONNECTED) closes. A type 5 received in EXPEDITED-DATA(CONNECTED) acknowledges nothing, since this node never sends type 4 (C-0276), and is ignored (C-0703)

source: Ed4 Tables C-22 and C-24; C.7.1.2; C.7.1.3
requirement: C-0738 sends a deferred EXPEDITED-ACK after leaving MANAGEMENT(CONNECTED) for DATA(CONNECTED), but DATA(CONNECTED) may not send type 5 (C-0746) and EXPEDITED-DATA(CONNECTED) may (C-0747). Reading: when the management exchange closes with a type 5 owed or a type 4 C_PDU partly received (a type 4 received in MANAGEMENT(CONNECTED), C-0722), the node goes to EXPEDITED-DATA(CONNECTED), and placing the type 5 then closes that state by C-1212; otherwise C-1212's target applies. A type 6 received in EXPEDITED-DATA(CONNECTED) deletes a partly reassembled type 4 C_PDU (C-0704, C-0761) and keeps a type 5 already owed, deferred as C-0722 defers one. The receiving side of the management exchange is finished when its acknowledgement is placed, as C-1070 reads it for the UNCONNECTED half

What happens to an owed type 5 when a RESET/WIN-RESYNC moves EXPEDITED-DATA(CONNECTED) to DATA(CONNECTED) or IDLE(CONNECTED) (C-0701, C-0736) is NOT STATED. Reading: the partly reassembled type 4 C_PDU is deleted (C-0761) and the unsent type 5 is dropped, since neither state sends type 5 (C-0745, C-0746); a type 4 the peer sends again draws a fresh one, and a copy of a delivered C_PDU is acknowledged again (C-1210)

How the allowed-type lists (C-0740 to C-0748) bind a transmission that also carries the D_PDU ending a state is NOT STATED. Reading: they are met by holding D_PDUs per peer in the planner. While a MANAGEMENT acknowledgement to the peer is unplaced, types 5, 7, 9, 10 and 11 to it wait (MANAGEMENT sends 6, 8, 13 to 15, C-0744, C-0748). While a type 5 to the peer is unplaced or a type 4 C_PDU from it is partly received, types 7, 9 and 11 wait (EXPEDITED-DATA(CONNECTED) sends 1, 4, 5, 8, 10, 13 to 15, C-0747). The D_PDUs that end those states go first in class order, so what they released may follow in the same transmission (C-1070, C-1129). RESET/WIN-RESYNC is not held: EXPEDITED-DATA(CONNECTED) may send it by C-0751, and in MANAGEMENT(CONNECTED) the acknowledgement that ends the state is placed ahead of it in class order (C-1174). The IDLE and DATA lists need no hold: a request moves IDLE to DATA or EXPEDITED-DATA before anything is sent (C-0655, C-0653, C-0656), and our own type 8 already holds data behind it (C-1044, C-1131)

source: Ed4 B.7.2.1 Step 2(d); Ed4 Table C-22
requirement: B-0403 counts a DATA C_PDU received through ARQ as the first data on a new link, written as D_UNIDATA_INDICATION with ARQ. Reading: a DATA C_PDU delivered by the expedited ARQ service (D_EXPEDITED_UNIDATA_INDICATION with ARQ, C-0702) counts too and stops cas.first_data, since it is a DATA C_PDU received over the link by ARQ (B-0215). Unlike non-ARQ data it uses the link: type 4 is connection-related, refused from an unconnected peer with WARNING reason 1 (C-0582) and taken only in the CONNECTED states (C-0662, C-0682), as the regular ARQ types are. Only a peer using the deprecated expedited data service sends one, since an Ed4 CAS sends DATA C_PDUs by the normal service (B-0115, A-0248)
notes: P4-6. Extends B-0403

requirement: GAP: whether a DATA-ONLY or DATA-ACK that fails one of Tests 1 to 5 still makes the move its state table row gives (IDLE(CONNECTED) to DATA(CONNECTED), C-0658, C-0660) is NOT STATED. Reading: it does not. C-1170 reads such a D_PDU as not used at all, and the move belongs to processing it; the FULL RESET it starts leaves IDLE(CONNECTED) as it is (C-0661). An ACK-ONLY in IDLE(CONNECTED) still goes to DATA(CONNECTED) with WARNING reason 3, since it is not tested (C-0659, C-1180)
notes: P4-7, from the P4-4 review (issue #45)

source: Ed4 C.4.8; Ed4 C.7.1.3; Ed4 Tables C-21, C-22
requirement: GAP: a receiver holding part of a type 4 C_PDU stays in EXPEDITED-DATA(CONNECTED) (C-1212), where types 9 and 11 may not be sent (C-0747, C-1215), so a peer that never finishes the C_PDU would stall our regular data, and no rule says when a partial C_PDU is given up. Reading: a DATA-ONLY or DATA-ACK of the link's family (types 9 and 11, or 0 and 2 on an 8-bit link) from the peer in a later received transmission than the partial C_PDU's last type 4 means the peer has abandoned it: the partial C_PDU is deleted and any type 5 still owed for it dropped, as C-1214 does, and EXPEDITED-DATA(CONNECTED) is left as C-1212 says. This holds whether or not the D_PDU is then used (sync tests, C-1175), since it is the peer's sending of it that shows the abandonment. A type 9 or 11 in the same transmission as the type 4s does not count: a compliant sender keeps its expedited C_PDU stop-and-wait (C-0756) but may place regular data after it. A transmission begins at each burst_started
notes: P4-7. Coordinator ruling 2026-11-07 (issue #45, from the P4-6 review)

requirement: GAP: C-0739 leaves what counts as DTS-detected link failure to the design. Reading: the DTS declares the connection lost once the peer has given no answer for 16 answer waits (16 x dts.ack_wait_ms, or 16 x the derived wait when that is unset; about 55 min at the 205.5 s default), timed only while an answer is awaited: from the end of the first of our transmissions after its last answer (or since the connection was made) that leaves dts.ack_wait or dts.reset_wait running for it, so a quiet spell with nothing awaited is never silence. It checks at each expiry of dts.ack_wait or dts.reset_wait for the peer, and at the end of each of our transmissions that carried a D_PDU to it, before any wait starts; a check that finds the bound reached loses the connection instead of retransmitting or repeating the command. An answer is a D_PDU from the peer that its ARQ machine acts on: a DATA-ONLY, ACK-ONLY or DATA-ACK that passes the synchronisation tests and is not discarded during a reset exchange (C-1175), a RESET/WIN-RESYNC that is acted on, or an EXPEDITED-DATA-ONLY. Other D_PDUs from the peer, such as a WARNING or a DATA-ONLY that fails the synchronisation tests, are not answers, so a reset exchange that never completes is covered (C-1172). The bound is time, not a count of waits, so a busy sender with a deep queue, whose waits are restarted by each retransmission round, still gives up a dead peer within it
notes: Issue #49: a reset that never completes is link failure. Issue #61: a count of 16 unanswered waits let a busy sender take hours or days to notice a dead peer (14.7 h with 400 U_PDUs queued in T3), so the coordinator ruled for a time bound of 16 answer waits. Across 5000 runs of the T3 ArqTransferTests at 15% block loss and 5% missed bursts the longest run of unanswered waits on a live link was 9 (P5-1); T4 may revise the bound. Issue #61 sweep: 1000 seeds of each ArqTransferTests variant passed with the time bound but the known seed 349; timing silence from the connection start instead of from an awaited answer lost a live 8-bit link (seed 845) at its first transmission after a quiet spell

source: Ed4 C.7.1.1 Figure C-54; C.7.5.2.1; Table C-1
requirement: The order of the DTS's own link termination is NOT STATED. Reading: D_CONNECTION_LOST goes to the CAS first, then ARQ processing stops and its variables reset, the peer goes to IDLE(UNCONNECTED), queued RESET/WIN-RESYNC and type 5 D_PDUs to it are withdrawn and every ARQ C_PDU not fully processed is rejected, oldest first, with a local reason (C-0866). The CAS then breaks the link locally (B-0324) and its D_CONNECTION_TERMINATED finds the peer unconnected and changes nothing (C-0572)

An explicit dts.ack_wait_ms shorter than csma.lbt_wait_dcd_ms makes a sender retransmit, again and again, before a peer that heard its transmission only in part may answer (C-1120 notes). Reading: such a configuration is refused when it is loaded, with a one-line error naming both settings; null (the derived wait) and any value at or above csma.lbt_wait_dcd_ms are accepted
notes: Coordinator ruling on issue #49 (b)

requirement: C-0851 puts higher priority first transmissions first only where that does not clash with in-order handling, and in order means in the order submitted (C-0017, A-0077), at DTS level across all SAPs (C-0018); how the planner keeps it is NOT STATED. Reading: an ARQ C_PDU with DELIVER IN ORDER is ordered among first transmissions by the highest priority of itself and of the in-order ARQ C_PDUs to the same peer queued after it that still have a segment to place, so in-order C_PDUs to one peer, of any SAP, get FSNs in submission order and a later one of higher priority takes the earlier ones ahead with it rather than overtaking them. The SIS hands U_PDUs held for a soft link down in arrival order, the in-order request being one of the implementation-dependent criteria with which it takes U_PDUs from its queues [p.A-22]
notes: Issue #72

requirement: NOT STATED: what a receiver does with complete in-order C_PDUs held behind a gap when the connection ends. Condition 2 of C-0178 can no longer be met, but their segments were acknowledged, which node delivery confirmation rests on [A.2.2.6 item 2 note], and ARQ guarantees the transfer of complete C_PDUs [C.2]. Reading: when the connection ends (D_CONNECTION_TERMINATED, or the DTS's own lost connection), before its state is reset, the DTS delivers the complete in-order C_PDUs it holds from the peer, in FSN order, with D_UNIDATA_INDICATION; partly received C_PDUs are lost. A FULL RESET still flushes them (C-0812). A sender that never saw the acknowledgement rejects the C_PDU (C-0866), and a client that sends it again may have it delivered twice
notes: Issue #71
